decisions.what: Routed the phase as medium complexity: two Hono routes, one React page, one gather module, plus navigation wiring across four registries (SYSTEM_PAGES, ROLE_LANES, ThreadView, server index).
decisions.why: Additive surface over an existing record primitive (UatSignoffRecorder) — no new node type, authority, or LLM — but it spans server + client + shared types + config, so not low.

decisions.what: Auto-approved the plan (6 tasks, 2 checkpoints, no unresolved concerns).
decisions.why: Task count < 15, complexity medium with no override, and the one build-time fork (the dashboard layer boundary) was resolved during brainstorming rather than left for planning.

decisions.what: Resolved the proposal's three Open Questions to their recommended defaults: change-level Success-Criteria basis (not engagement/BRD roll-up), an explicit ?slug query param (no picker), and a free-text signer identity.
decisions.why: Each recommended default keys off an acceptance basis already on disk and already wired to the node; the deferred engagement/BRD roll-up needs change->BRD traceability plumbing that does not exist yet and warrants its own #710-follow-up.

decisions.what: Reused UatSignoffRecorder verbatim as the sole write path; the POST route records the identical execution_outcome node the uat_signoff MCP tool records.
decisions.why: Spec Decision 1 — a second record path would fork the acceptance history. A browser sign-off and a CLI sign-off must be the same node.

decisions.what: Opened the dashboard architecture layer to depend on `intelligence` (harness.config.json allowedDependencies += intelligence; package.json += workspace dep).
decisions.why: The mandated recorder reuse lives in the intelligence layer, which the dashboard layer did not previously permit. Verified the layer-violations collector skips bare @harness-engineering/* specifiers (external imports resolve to null), so the change is honest declaration, not a new arch-gate regression.

decisions.what: Kept the acceptance-basis extraction self-contained in gather/signoff.ts (a fenced-code-aware fallback-chain parser) rather than importing outcome-eval's internal section-resolver.
decisions.why: The resolver is not exported from the intelligence barrel; re-deriving the same Success-Criteria -> User-Visible Behavior -> Overview soft-degrade locally avoids coupling to an internal and keeps the surface's read path independent of the eval contract.

decisions.what: Enforced the skill's Iron Law at the write boundary: the POST rejects a missing overall verdict, a missing signer, or any item lacking a disposition with a 4xx and records nothing.
decisions.why: The human is the sole authority; the surface must never infer a verdict. Covering test posts each malformed body and asserts an unchanged graph plus no signoff.md.

decisions.what: Left the sign-off route free of any gate/CI/pipeline import and pinned it with a module-dependency test.
decisions.why: AC-9 — the record blocks nothing. UAT stays advisory / human-judged, distinct from the blocking, LLM-judged acceptance-eval / outcome-eval contracts.

decisions.what: Tightened the AC-9 dependency test to scan import statements only, after it initially flagged the sibling-contract names in explanatory prose comments.
decisions.why: The comments legitimately name outcome-eval / acceptance-eval to draw the distinction; the observable guarantee is about imports, not prose.
